We learn TT through its Cholesky factor LL (Eq. (10)). To keep TT well-conditioned, we optionally clamp the diagonal of LL (equivalently the eigenvalues of TT) within a reasonable range; such conditioning controls are not required by the theory (Eq. (6)) but improve robustness in large-scale pretraining. Regularizers on logdetT\log\det T or on ‖log⁡diag⁡(L)‖\|\log\mathrm{diag}(L)\| can be added as optional stabilizers; by default we rely on the SPD parameterization and standard optimization.

To stay consistent with standard weight tying practices, we can checkpoint only (Z,T)(Z,T) (and the fixed QQ if diag_basis is used) and reconstruct EE and WoutW_{\mathrm{out}} on load using Eq. (4). This reduces redundant storage and keeps the tying relationship explicit.

While PIT can be extended to a higher-dimensional shared memory (e.g., Z∈ℝV×mZ\in\mathbb{R}^{V\times m} with m>dm>d), in this work we fix m=dm=d for simplicity and fair comparison to standard language models: (i) it keeps the embedding/head dimensionality unchanged; (ii) it preserves the asymptotic cost of the vocabulary projection; and (iii) it avoids introducing extra capacity that could confound the effect of pseudo-inverse tying.
